final_response:
Revised registration screen specification, v1. Current phase: **registration**. Preserve the existing visual identity and the liked treatments in images 1–6, using image 7 for the overall layout.

The screen should help an operator find a person, inspect registration details and resume unfinished registration work.

1. **Sidebar:** Keep the existing navigation treatment and icons. “Registration desk” remains visibly active without a notification dot. Place the sole profile control at the bottom left.
2. **Header:** Keep the desk context and the outlined “Escalations” and “Desk help” buttons from image 2.
3. **Page heading:** Keep “Registration desk.” Use registration-focused supporting copy, such as “Find a person or continue an unfinished registration.” Keep the “Record donation” treatment from image 3.
4. **Search and unfinished work:** Retain the two-column desktop arrangement. The search form keeps First name, Last name, Phone, Email (optional), Search Records and its existing Clear control. The adjacent In progress panel keeps useful registration blockers and existing Continue/Edit actions.
5. **Results:** Preserve readable person rows and registration-relevant details. Keep the result count and existing permitted result controls. Selection uses a checkbox and an even border around the entire row.
6. **Selection actions:** Keep Clear selection, which deselects people without changing their records. Retain “Continue with selected” only if its existing destination belongs to registration; its destination needs verification.

| Source | Decision | Acceptance check |
|---|---|---|
| Image 1 | Change selected navigation | Active treatment and icon remain; notification dot is absent. |
| Image 2 | Keep help buttons | Escalations and Desk help retain their outlined treatment; no additional help features appear. |
| Image 3 | Keep Record donation | Existing action and styling remain; no payment behavior is invented. |
| Image 4 | Remove Filter: All Attendees | Remove the label and dropdown together. No replacement tabs, chips or filter appear. |
| Image 4 / full screen | Keep search fields | All four fields remain independently labeled and usable after tab removal. |
| Image 5 | Add View all in progress | Place the action beside the panel heading. It exposes all unfinished registrations within the existing authorized scope, with a visible return to the desk. |
| Image 5 | Add a pending-work clear action | Its object, saved effects and recovery must be resolved as decision C1 below. |
| Image 6 | Change selected row | Use the same border weight on all four sides, retaining existing rounding. Remove the thick left accent. Keep checkbox and keyboard focus distinct. |
| Image 6 | Remove Query: Test | No decorative query chip repeats the search input. |
| Image 7 | Remove Synced to event sheet | Routine sync text disappears; actionable failures still appear beside affected work. |
| Explicit instruction | One profile location | Desktop profile exists only at bottom left. The supplied full screen does not visibly show the reported top-right duplicate; remove it wherever present in the implementation. |
| Image 7 | Remove counters | Checked In and In Queue counters are absent. |
| Image 7 | Remove search tabs | Name / Phone, Scan QR and Family ID tabs are absent. |
| Image 7 | Remove device panel | Printer and badge-stock panel disappear without a replacement status widget. |
| Current phase | Exclude check-in content throughout | Remove Quick Check-In, the In Queue row badge, Badge printed and the badge-print instruction in the selection bar from registration UI. |

Use the existing components, icon family, typography, colors, spacing and rounding. The screenshots establish visual treatment, not exact token values. Registration component source and exact tokens were not supplied; do not guess a font, palette or spacing scale.

For narrower layouts, preserve reading order: heading, search, In progress, results and contextual selection actions. Stack related fields when needed, let row actions wrap, and keep long names and essential details readable. A fixed selection bar must reserve sufficient content space so it cannot cover rows, errors or keyboard focus. The account control remains in the navigation area without a second header copy.

The affected states need these behaviors:

- **Search:** distinguish initial, searching, results, no matches and failure. Keep criteria editable after no matches or an error. Announce results without moving focus.
- **In progress:** support zero, one and many unfinished registrations. Saved unfinished work displays remaining tasks, not a spinner. Show “View all in progress” consistently when work exists; make all records reachable without introducing filters or bulk actions.
- **Registration actions:** show truthful submitting and failure feedback where those actions already exist. Prevent duplicate submissions and preserve valid input where supported.
- **Selection:** show selected count and checked controls, with an independent focus indicator. Clear selection changes selection only.
- **Exit and recovery:** the expanded unfinished-work view has a visible return route. Existing edit flows must explain any unsaved-work consequences before navigation.

Use native labeled controls, logical heading and keyboard order, accessible names for icon controls, and text alongside status colors. Verify text contrast of 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text and required control boundaries; pointer targets of at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels or an applicable exception; 200% text resizing; and reflow at 320 CSS pixels.

**Needs approval before build:** C1 concerns the pending-work clear action. My proposal is **“Dismiss from this desk” for one card**, leaving the saved registration intact and still reachable through View all in progress. This is a proposal, not approved behavior. Specify whether dismissal lasts for the current session or persists before implementation. Abandoning drafts or deleting records requires a separate explicit choice. The ui-ux-design operating contract requires this distinction because “clear” does not establish what happens to saved work.

**Unresolved classification:** The reference does not establish whether “Fast Track” or “Continue with selected” performs a registration action. Confirm their existing destinations; preserve registration behavior and defer check-in behavior. Do not silently repurpose either action.

Later-phase notes contain QR lookup, Family ID lookup, check-in counters and actions, queue status, badge printing and device monitoring. Do not create placeholders, hidden routes or supporting models for them in this phase.

| Handoff check | Status | Evidence / next action |
|---|---|---|
| Screen context | Pass | Registration job, sources and exact corrections are recorded. |
| Design direction | Pass | Preserve the supplied identity and liked treatments. |
| Hierarchy | Pass | Lookup and unfinished registration work lead the specification. |
| States / F3 | Not verified | States are specified; resolve C1 and verify actual save/recovery behavior. |
| Integrity / F2 | Not verified | Exact source tokens and the two legacy action destinations need inspection. |
| Navigation / F1 | Pass | Safe return and unsaved-work requirements are specified; runtime remains untested. |
| Accessibility | Not verified | Criteria are specified; rendered and interaction tests are still required. |
| Motion | Not applicable | No motion change is requested. |
| Content and density | Not verified | Responsive rules are specified; test rendered zero/one/many and difficult content. |
| Handoff | Pass | Scope, exclusions, feedback coverage and open decisions are explicit. |

The specification is complete for review. Implementation readiness depends on C1 and the legacy-action classification. No application or pack files were changed.
evidence_limits: The registration screen evidence consisted of the six supplied crops and the full-screen image.
The inspected existing.html file was an unrelated invoice fixture and did not establish registration component values or behavior.
No registration implementation source, updated rendered screen, or runtime interaction evidence was available.
No runtime keyboard, focus, assistive-technology, persistence, permission, contrast, or responsive testing was performed.
The meaning and persistence of pending-work clear, and the destinations of Fast Track and Continue with selected, were not established by the supplied evidence.
